content.comment_body: Hello! I'm wondering if the outputs on the [product_name] module are current-limited. When I connected a 0.8A load to one of the outputs, the current measured was 0.3A, which matches the technical specifications in the datasheet for [product_name]. At other hardware platforms, connecting too large a load can permanently damage the output, but that doesn't seem to be the case here. Can someone confirm whether this output is really current-limited as described? Regards, [user_name]

Hi, According to the technical details in the [product_name] manual: Output voltage is less than the supply voltage, Current output is 0.3A per channel, There is short-circuit protection, and short-circuit limitation is about 1A. Based on this, my understanding is that the maximum output current per channel is limited to 0.3A.

It appears that way since the module won't supply more than 0.3A, even though my connected device required 0.8A. And yes, I know on some platforms, connecting a bigger load can result in destroyed outputs, but I was just curious to test it here.

The manual claims there is protection, but in real use, there is not! If you connect a load that is much too high, the transistor output gets damaged instantly. The documentation isn't accurate in this regard. I have contacted [company_name] about it and hope future manuals or the next version of [product_name] address this issue.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are discussing whether the transistor outputs in [product_name] modules are truly current-limited and provide effective short-circuit protection. Conflicting reports between manual descriptions and users' actual experiences have led to confusion, particularly since some users mention outputs being damaged despite claimed protections. This mismatch is creating uncertainty and reducing trust in the product documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that [product_name] transistor outputs will limit current or provide reliable short-circuit protection, preventing damage when loads exceed the maximum specified value.
